title: Skin phase transition of a skyrmion in a ferromagnetic superfluid
authors: Wooyoung Yun, Se Kwon Kim, Hiromitsu Takeuchi
abstract: Compared with a scalar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), a spinor BEC supports richer phenomena because of its internal spin degrees of freedom, including topological solitons such as domain walls or skyrmions. Here, we theoretically reveal three distinct axisymmetric soliton structures formed as a circular domain wall in a spin-1 BEC, connected within fixed winding numbers. We refer to these structures as the broken-axisymmetry (BA)-skin, antiferromagnetic (AF)-skin and normal-core phases. Their occurrence is controlled by the two dimensionless parameters in the absence of linear Zeeman coefficient $p=0$: $q/μ$, the ratio of the quadratic Zeeman coefficient to the chemical potential, and $c_s/c_n$, the ratio of spin interaction to the density interaction. The BA-skin and AF-skin phases exhibit local easy-plane magnetic order and local easy-plane spin-nematic order, respectively, while the normal-core phase is similar to a doubly quantized vortex analogous to that of a scalar BEC with a density depletion at the center. We obtain semi-analytical estimates of selected transition boundaries separating these phases by analyzing the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equation and also numerically confirm them by solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. We estimate the skyrmion radius using a hydrostatic approximation and compare the result with numerical solutions. We envision our results on skyrmions in a spin-1 BEC can trigger further investigation on novel soliton structures in a magnetic superfluid.
summary: This theoretical study maps out the complex phase diagram of skyrmion structures in a ferromagnetic spin-1 Bose-Einstein Condensate. By analyzing the Gross-Pitaevskii equation and its stability spectrum, the authors predict continuous transitions between BA-skin and AF-skin phases, alongside a discontinuous transition to a normal-core vortex state. This work advances the understanding of topological matter in quantum gases.
main_problem: The paper investigates the skin phase transition of a skyrmion within a ferromagnetic superfluid realized in a spin-1 Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC). It specifically analyzes the transition between three distinct soliton structures: BA-skin, AF-skin, and normal-core phases.
main_result: The skyrmion structure undergoes continuous phase transitions between the BA-skin and AF-skin phases, controlled by the quadratic Zeeman coefficient ratio ($q/\mu$). Furthermore, a discontinuous transition to a normal-core (Nc) vortex phase is predicted.
method: The study employs theoretical analysis using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) equation to estimate transition boundaries, complemented by numerical solutions of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GPE) for confirmation.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1 BEC, whose dynamics are governed by the GPE. The physics is controlled by dimensionless parameters, notably $q/\mu$ (quadratic Zeeman ratio) and $c_s/c_n$ (spin interaction ratio), under the assumption of zero linear Zeeman coefficient ($p=0$).
key_observables: The primary observables are the spatial profiles of the order parameter amplitude ($f_m(r)$) and the existence/nature of the skin structure (BA-skin vs. AF-skin).
important_parameters: The key controlling parameters are $q/\mu$ and $c_s/c_n$. The analysis focuses on the ferromagnetic regime ($c_s < 0$ and $q < 0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes rotational symmetry and utilizes the GPE framework. Specific approximations include using the BdG equation for stability analysis and the hydrostatic approximation for radius estimation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural differences between BA-skin and AF-skin phases at different $q/\mu$ values. Other figures map out the phase boundaries in the parameter space ($q/\mu$ vs. $c_s/c_n$) and show hysteresis loops characterizing the BA-Nc transition.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework and identifying the three soliton phases. It then uses the BdG equation to analyze the continuous BA-AF transition and subsequently investigates the more complex, potentially discontinuous, transitions involving the normal-core phase.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it explores topological defects (skyrmions) in ultracold atomic systems (BECs). The detailed phase diagram mapping and stability analysis provide concrete, predictive tools for controlling exotic quantum states in magnetic superfluids.
